Alappuzha, where the prosecution alleges commission of offences under Sections 498A and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant documents.
3. The prosecution case in a nutshell is that the 1 st accused married the defacto complainant on 17.03.2022 and they resided together at the matrimonial home.
Thereafter, the accused herein subjected her to cruelty demanding more dowry and also by insulting her stating that the amount given at the time of marriage was much less.

The further allegation is that the 1st accused misrepresented his job as 'Third Officer' in Merchant Navy, though he is only a Salesman much lower in rank than that of a 'Third Officer' and thereby cheated the defacto complainant.

4. In fact, this application originally filed on 13.02.2024 and this Court referred the parties for mediation, but the mediation was not successful, even though part of the gold ornaments were agreed to be received by the defacto complainant.
Therefore, regarding the other claims, the defacto complainant can proceed against the accused under law.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners are innocent and the allegations are false.
Accordingly, offering co-operation in the matter of investigation, anticipatory bail is sought for.

6. The learned counsel for the defacto complainant strongly opposed bail, highlighting the cheating at the instance of the 1st accused by misrepresenting a higher rank as a 'Third Officer' in Merchant Navy, where actually, the 1 st accused is only a Salesman.
He also submitted that the mediation attempt failed.

7. Although the learned Public Prosecutor opposed bail, on perusal of prosecution records, general allegations of cruelty during stay of the couples at the matrimonial home is the crux of the dispute.
Further cheating by misrepresentation is the other allegation.
Therefore, investigation is possible even without custodial interrogation.
8. Having considered the factual matrix of the case in the above line, I am of the view that the petitioners deserve anticipatory bail.
Thus, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail, with direction to the petitioners to co-operate with the investigation.
Therefore, this petition stands allowed.

The petitioners are enlarged on anticipatory bail on the following conditions:
i.
The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer within ten days from today and on such surrender, the Investigating Officer can question the petitioners and record their statement.
In the event of their arrest, the Investigating Officer shall produce the petitioners before the Jurisdictional Court on the date of arrest itself.

ii. On such production, Jurisdictional Court shall release the petitioners on bail, on executing bond for Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand) each by themselves and by Sahsad Koya Thangal vs State Of Kerala on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83738633/
